g: Grilling round 3, updated after your note (2026-10-14): residents create gold by using Goods; Towns pay the Crown on trade

q: Towns pay the 30% Tariff out of their own Purse (it is no longer new gold). Your note says a self-sufficient Town that only sells brings the Crown 0%, which means the BUYING Town pays. Is that right?
ctx: Then a Town earns by selling and by its residents using Goods, and pays the Crown whenever it buys from another Town.
o: Yes: the buying Town pays the price plus 30% on top; the seller keeps the whole price
No: the selling Town pays 30% out of the sale

q: Residents create gold for their Town each time they use a Good (Tax is new gold made this way). How much per unit used?
ctx: Example with the first choice: a Hut's Peasants pay 1.5 × 4 = 6 gold for each Potato they eat. If the Town bought that Potato for 5 gold, it earns 1 gold; if it paid 8, it loses 2.
o: A fixed amount per Good: 1.5 × its base price for a Basic Need, 2 × for a Luxury. Market prices decide whether buying a Good in to supply residents earns or loses the Town money
The Good's current global price × 1.5 (Luxury × 2): supplying residents almost always pays

q: "A Good's price is global, and each Town adjusts its own price on top." How does the global price move?
o: It doesn't: the global price is the Good's base price; only each Town's own adjustment (its Stock and Sales pressure) moves
It follows the whole Kingdom's supply and demand (lots of Stock everywhere = cheaper), and each Town adjusts on top

q: Buyers take whatever is available if they can afford it. When several Towns sell the same Good, which one does the buyer go to?
o: The nearest one that has enough (shortest trip)
The one with the most spare Stock (today's rule)
